user.title: Boiler Monitor
user.description: Choose the entity that tells when the burner is firing, plus the optional temperature sensors. Every sensor except the burner is optional; features that need a missing sensor are simply not created.

data_description.name: A name for this boiler. It is used for the device and for the entity IDs, e.g. "Centrala" creates sensor.centrala_status.
data_description.burner_entity: The entity that is ON while the burner fires (or while there is heat demand). It can be a switch (e.g. the ESPHome relay that drives the boiler), a binary_sensor (flame), an input_boolean, a climate entity (its hvac_action is used) or a sensor with a text state.
data_description.burner_on_state: The exact state that means "burner on". Use "on" for switch / binary_sensor / input_boolean, "heating" for a climate entity, or the exact text of a sensor's state.
data_description.flow_temp_entity: Temperature of the hot water leaving the boiler towards the radiators, in °C. Needed for the flow-return ΔT.
data_description.return_temp_entity: Temperature of the water coming back from the radiators into the boiler, in °C. Needed for the condensing ratio and the "Condensation lost" alert.
data_description.flow_setpoint_entity: The flow temperature the boiler is aiming for, in °C – e.g. "Ariston CH flow setpoint temp". With automatic thermoregulation ON it follows the weather-compensation curve; with it OFF it is the fixed flow temperature you set. Enables flow-vs-target and the heating-curve chart.
data_description.thermoregulation_entity: The switch that turns the boiler's weather compensation on/off – e.g. "Ariston automatic thermoregulation". ON = the flow target follows the outdoor temperature (curve); OFF = fixed flow temperature. The card and charts adapt to the mode.
data_description.outdoor_temp_entity: Outside air temperature, in °C. Needed for the outdoor correlation, balance point and burn hours per degree-day.
data_description.indoor_temp_entities: One or more room temperature sensors, in °C. Their average (unavailable sensors are skipped) is used to check whether heating actually warms the house.
data_description.thermostat_entity: The climate entity that decides when to heat, e.g. your Generic Thermostat. Its target temperature is the comfort reference: needed for the comfort-vs-outdoor verdict and the pre-heat time. If no indoor sensors are set, its current temperature is used as the room temperature.
data_description.weather_entity: A weather entity with an hourly forecast (e.g. Tomorrow.io). Used by the estimate_preheat action to take the forecast outdoor temperature into account. Optional.
data_description.pressure_entity: Water pressure of the heating circuit, in bar – e.g. "Ariston heating circuit pressure". Enables the low/high pressure alert and the 7-day pressure trend (slow leak detection). Monitored all year.
data_description.season_entity: Optional. While this entity is NOT in the state below, monitoring is paused (no cycles counted, no alerts) – useful in summer when the boiler only makes hot water. Leave empty to monitor all year.
data_description.season_state: The state of the heating-season entity that means "heating season active", e.g. "on" (input_boolean / switch), "heat" (climate) or the exact option text of an input_select. Ignored if no heating-season entity is selected.

abort.already_configured: This burner entity is already monitored.

data_description.short_cycle_minutes: In minutes. If the burner starts again sooner than this after it stopped, the start is counted as a short cycle and an alert is raised. Default 10 min.
data_description.return_threshold: In °C. Above this return temperature a condensing boiler stops condensing and loses efficiency (≈ 55 °C for natural gas). Default 53 °C.
data_description.return_hot_minutes: In minutes. How long the return must stay above the threshold, while the burner is on, before the "Condensation lost" alert is raised. Short peaks are ignored. Default 15 min.
data_description.effect_check_minutes: In minutes. How long after the burner starts the room temperatures are checked again to see if they rose. Use 30–45 for radiators, 90–120 for underfloor heating. Default 45 min.
data_description.min_temp_rise: In °C. If the average room temperature rose less than this after the check delay, "Heating ineffective" is raised (e.g. air in radiators, closed valves, flow too cold). Default 0.2 °C.
data_description.min_burn_seconds: In seconds. Burns shorter than this are treated as relay glitches or failed ignitions and are removed completely from the statistics. Default 20 s.
data_description.pressure_min: In bar. Below this the "Pressure problem" alert is raised (refill the system). Typical cold pressure is 1.0–1.5 bar. Default 1.0 bar.
data_description.pressure_max: In bar. Above this the "Pressure problem" alert is raised (expansion vessel / over-filling). The safety valve opens around 3 bar. Default 2.5 bar.
data_description.notify_service: Where to send push alerts, e.g. notify.mobile_app_my_phone (or a notify entity). Leave empty for no push notifications – events and binary sensors work either way. Max one alert per hour per type.
data_description.csv_log: When on, every START / STOP / SHORT_CYCLE / RETURN_HOT / INEFFECTIVE event is appended to a CSV file in /config/boiler_monitor/ (one file per boiler).

entry_id.name: Entry ID
entry_id.description: Limit to these config entries (empty = all).

estimate_preheat.name: Estimate pre-heat
estimate_preheat.description: Estimates how long the house needs to warm up to a temperature and when heating should start. Returns a response for use in automations.

target_temperature.name: Target temperature
target_temperature.description: Room temperature to reach, in °C (default: the thermostat's current target).

at.name: At
at.description: Time the target must be reached (e.g. 07:00). Without it, only the duration is returned.
